title: 2xLampa Bactericid BSR-02 15W cu stativ telescopic si timer
description:
Lampa Bactericid BSR-02 15 W produsa de ELBA este folosita pentru dezinfectarea aerului, a apei şi a suprafeţelor din spitale, laboratoare de cercetare bacteriologică şi medii farmaceutice, cabinete medicale, săli de clasa, industria alimentară și hotelieră, spaţii de depozitare alimente, ambalaje pentru alimente, săli de mese etc. Soluțiile de dezinfectare pe bază de radiație UV-C sunt utilizate ca parte a ciclului de dezinfecție / sterilizare și au ca scop prevenirea și reducerea răspândirii bolilor infecțioase, a virușilor, bacteriilor și a altor tipuri de microorganisme dăunătoare, în special în unitățile medicale. Lampa Bactericid BSR-02 15 W : • Este formată dintr-o carcasă din tablă de oţel sudată şi vopsită alb (exterior) • Asigura dezinfectarea unei suprafaţe efectivă 6-8 m², volum efectiv sterilizat 18m³; • Reflector din tablă de aluminiu oglindată cu coeficient de reflexie >0.85; • Este prevăzută cu o articulaţie ce permite rotirea în jurul unei axe paralele cu tubul fluorescent. Acest fapt permite direcţionarea fluxului radiaţiei UV pe anumite zone din încăperea în care se dorește dezinfectarea ; • Pentru a permite o orientare şi în plan orizontal corpul este montat pe un trepied – astfel poate fi apropiat de suprafeţele ce trebuie dezinfectate; • Aparatajul (balastul) este inclus în produs şi executat în conformitate cu normativele specifice. Pachetul contine 2xLampa Bactericid BSR-02 15 W, stativul telescopic si timer-ul

title: Germany – Environmental issues consultancy services – 81309020-Development of Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (MER) Systems for Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) in India
description: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), GmbH - India is implementing a six-year project titled "Restore, Conserve and Protect Forest and Tree Cover for NDC Implementation in India (RECAP4NDC)" under Indo-German bilateral cooperation. The Indian political partner is the Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India. The project involves a consortium of six partners, including GIZ, International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) India, Forest Survey of India (FSI), The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI), Indian Council for Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE), and International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD). The project aims to support India in achieving its targets on restoring degraded forests and landscapes inside and outside forests as defined in the National Forest Policy and the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC"s). The approach aligns with the principles of the Bonn Challenge, focusing on restoring the ecological functionality of degraded landscapes while enhancing the well-being of people. By 2029, RECAP4NDC aims to achieve ecological, socio-economic, governance, and climate change benefits across 0.4 million hectares of forest landscape, benefiting 10 million people through improved forest ecosystem services. Four states have been selected for cooperation, each with specific starting conditions: - Delhi NCR: Faces challenges of rapid urban development and encroachment, with potential for urban tree cover restoration and cross-agency collaboration. - Gujarat: Includes diverse habitats like grasslands, mangroves and hill ranges, requiring unique restoration approaches for coastal degradation and grazing pressures. - Maharashtra: Features nine agro-climatic zones, providing opportunities for comparative testing of different FLR approaches. - Uttarakhand: Has a range of elevation zones, with existing community forestry programmes that can be supplemented with targeted interventions. Implementing partners are State Forest Departments (SFD) of the respective states. Project outputs are divided among consortium partners and include FLR model implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting (MER) systems, financing models for FLR, policy and planning integration, and capacity building for stakeholders. The assignment is to be carried out in close coordination with FSI, who has responsibility for the MER output. The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this contract focus on developing an integrated MER system to assess the ecological, economic, and social impacts of FLR initiatives. The assignment has three main objectives: - Develop and refine digital monitoring and evaluation systems and tools for FLR. - Build stakeholder capacities through targeted training and development programmes. - Design and deploy adaptive and scalable reporting frameworks for FLR impacts. This project will strengthen MER systems for FLR reporting in India, supporting transparent communication of FLR impacts to inform policy and practice. It aims to develop and refine monitoring and evaluation tools that accurately measure the ecological, economic, and social impacts of Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) initiatives at various governance levels. The objective is to create monitoring systems, including protocols, measuring tools, guidelines, and frameworks, to generate reliable data that aids decision-makers in setting priorities, making informed decisions, and improving inter-departmental coordination. These systems will help report on national and international targets and commitments and be adaptable to the dynamic landscapes and diverse needs of FLR projects in India. it will incorporate existing monitoring tools and frameworks of key implementing partners at the state level, such as SFDs and other line departments, and national reporting mechanisms implemented by FSI and MoEFCC.

title: HIGH FREQUENCY AIRBORNE RADIOMETER INSTRUMENT FOR THE SUPPORT OF FUTURE ALTIMETRY MISSIONS
description: Satellite altimetry plays an essential role in producing sea level and waves products such as sea surface height (SSH), significantwave height (SWH), mean sea level and near surface wind/wave products.Today, a low frequency channel microwave radiometer is in general used to correct the altimeter range for water vapor path delay over ocean. The wet tropospheric correction (WTC) is consideredas one of the largest source of uncertainty in sea level estimate. As any artificial temporal drift in the wet tropospheric correction translate immediately to a similar drift in the mean sea level, there is a need for extremely well calibrated radiometer instrument to retrieve this wet tropospheric correction in support of the accurate altimeter measurement. Depending on the targeted temporal and spatial scales, some recent studies and projects ("Radiometer Instrument for Swath Altimeter missions", Sentinel-6 HRMR instrument, Sentinel-3 NG-T) have shown that the two existing classes of satellite altimeters such as the conventional nadir looking altimeters and the wide swath altimeters would both benefit from the addition of one or several high frequency channels (89/165/172 GHz)to the low frequency channels (18.7/23.8/36.5(or 31.4) GHz) already used for the WTC retrieval. The advantages brought by the addition of the high frequency channels in the microwave radiometer are several fold. For a given RF radiating aperture, the high frequency radiometer would exhibit a high spatial resolution and therefore shall be less prone to land contamination in coastal areas that would directly impact the uncertainty of the WTC based on brightness temperature measurement near the coastline. For wide swath altimeters, a multibeam microwave radiometer combining the low and high frequency channels would help to retrieve the WTC across-track with an increased accuracy and with better spatial resolution commensurate with the high spatial resolution radar retrievals from a swath altimeter. Moreover, the high frequency channels (typically 89 GHz or 165/172 GHz) can provide additional information for precipitation screening.This new proposed activity aims at developing an airborne demonstrator instrument to validate the benefits of thehigh frequency radiometer measurement, to support the continued improvement of the altimeter measurement and observation capabilities. The activity shall start with the detailed analysis of user requirements and the design of the instrument, then continue with themanufacturing, integration and test of the airborne system and finally concludes with the airworthiness certification on an airborne carrier and a functional test flight to validate the airborne radiometer function and performance and collect first experimental data.

description: Objective: The objective is to design, develop and test an Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system onboard the satellite for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offeringreliable AIS information with low-latency.TargetedImprovements: Reduce by half the latency of detection of non-reliable reporting vessels compared to current technologies. Decrease reliance on ground-based infrastructures by enabling onboarddetection of deceptive AIS signals.Description: With approximately 90% of international trade travelling by sea, maritime routes are becoming increasingly congested. A reliable maritime domain awareness is thus paramount toaddress critical security (e.g. submarine cables, piracy), safety (e.g. collision avoidance), economic (e.g. fleet monitoring) or environmental (e.g. illegal fishing) needs, and space-basedcomponents are critical due to the limited terrestrial systems coverage. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is one of the main components of the current maritime domain awarenessinfrastructure, being mandated by International Maritime Organisation and enabling the reporting of vessels worldwide. However, the current AIS setup suffers from reliability issues.Vessels can arbitrarily either switch off their AIS transponder or use (or being the target of) malicious deceiving techniques such as AIS spoofing and jamming or manipulation of GNSSinformation embedded in such messages. This results in fictitious abnormal behaviours that are becoming increasingly common and causing significant disruption across entire regions.Moreover, traditional satellite-based AIS processing systems rely heavily on ground-based validation, leading to high latency in spoofing detection and reducing the effectiveness of real timecountermeasures.An onboard detection module could overcome these challenges by detecting in near real-time any AIS anomaly and initiate the mitigation countermeasures, i.e. paired with communicationto other trailing satellites or direct-to-device communication links (out of the scope of this activity), such detection system could inform users about fraudulent activities faster thantraditional surveillance systems.This activity will develop and test an onboard Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offering reliableAIS informationwith low-latency. Low latency AI-based anomaly detection and other technologies such as signal fingerprinting and deterministic algorithms will be investigated and developed.The AIS spoofing detection module shall be designed according to selecteduse cases and implemented on a software-defined radio-based payload and tested in a representativemaritime surveillance scenario to evaluate its effectiveness in detecting, localising, and mitigating AIS spoofing in real time.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. title: Dodávka kamerového systému pro posílení bezpečnostních prvků v budově CS, CU, ZO a ZY Ostravské univerzity — část 1: Dodávka kamer pro posílení bezpečnostních prvků v budově CS, CU, ZO a ZY OU
description: Předmětem části 1 veřejné zakázky je dodávka kamer za účelem posílení bezpečnostních prvků v budovách CS, CU, ZO a ZY Ostravské univerzity. V případě budov CS a CU zahrnuje předmět plnění dodávku, montáž, instalaci, uvedení kamer do provozu – do stavu plné využitelnosti jejich technických parametrů vč. dalšího potřebného nastavení dle pokynů výrobce a provedení kamerové zkoušky. Montáž kamer bude provedená v souladu s Přílohou č. 3 - Projektovou dokumentací, která specifikuje umístění jednotlivých kamer. (Poznámka: V projektové dokumentaci pro budovu CU jsou kamery určené k dodání vyznačeny žlutou a modrou barvou, stávající kamery jsou vyznačeny červenou barvou, fialová čára – vedení UTP, modrý čtvereček – UTP zásuvka) Zadavatel upozorňuje, že v případě budovy CS je pro instalaci venkovních kamer zapotřebí plošina, kterou si zajistí dodavatel na své náklady (výška spodního zrcadla oblouku na CS je 12,7 m nad zpevněnou plochou). K instalaci vnitřních kamer v budově CS (konkrétně kamery č. 23 a 24) bude dodavateli po dobu realizace plnění z titulu výpůjčky, tedy bezplatně, vypůjčena zdvihací pracovní plošina (elektrická teleskopická plošina GTWY 14-200 DC s baterií [pracovní dosah 14 m, nosnost 200 kg]), která je dle nařízení vlády č. 193/2022 Sb., ve znění pozdějších předpisů vyhrazeným zdvihacím zařízením a vyžaduje kvalifikovanou obsluhu. V případě budov ZO a ZY je předmětem plnění pouze dodávka kamer, bez jejich instalace či zprovoznění. Bližší podrobnosti vztahující se k předmětu veřejné zakázky jsou uvedeny v této zadávací dokumentaci, formuláři Nabídka, obchodních podmínkách a přílohách.
